FLASHCARD SET · AGES 3–4 YEARS

Fruit & Vegetable Flashcards for Preschoolers

Sixteen cards about the foods children see every day: eight fruits, eight vegetables, every one right here with the words to say together and one thing to try at snack time.

THE CARDS

Every card in the set.

Every card is right here on one page: the picture and short, practical notes for grown-ups — what it is for, how to use it, how to print it. Read every card right here.

HOW TO USE THESE CARDS

Four ways that work.

You do not need a plan or a printer schedule. Pick one idea, try it for two minutes and see what happens.

  1. 01

    Name it, then find it in the kitchen

    The pair is the whole lesson: “apple!” — then hunt the fruit bowl together. The word sticks when the real food lands in your child’s hand.

  2. 02

    Sort the cards, then sort the snack

    Fruit cards on one plate, vegetable cards on another — then do it for real with an apple and a carrot. Sorting food is a game children can eat.

  3. 03

    Play the color rows

    Which foods are red? Which are green? Lay the cards out in color rows together — the kitchen becomes a rainbow.

  4. 04

    Take one card shopping

    Hand your child the carrot card at the market and let them find its twin in the pile. One matched carrot is a whole class.

      Apple Flashcard for Preschoolers

      A shiny red apple with a leaf still on — the fruit most children name first. The word apple sits under it, and there is probably one within reach of your kitchen right now.

      Download card ↓

      Teaching tips

      What this card does

      Names the fruit most children already own, and gives the crunch a word.

      At the table

      Cut one round slice and find the star hiding in the middle.

      What it teaches

      First fruit words stick fastest to fruit already in the house.

      Getting it on paper

      Print on card stock; this card leads a working life.

      Tip for today

      The star needs a grown-up knife and a very flat slice.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Apple lesson on the Learning Path.

      One word, two lessons

      This card names the fruit for naming. Learning letter sounds too? The letter A lesson teaches the /a/ sound step by step — and at lunchtime the same apple has a Cafeteria page on a sixty-two-food tray.

      FLASHCARD · FRUITS & VEGETABLES FLASHCARDS · AGES 3–4 YEARS

      Banana Flashcard for Preschoolers

      A cheerful yellow banana, curved like a smile. The word banana sits under it — a long word that children love to stretch: ba-na-na!

      Download card ↓

      Teaching tips

      What this card does

      Puts the word on the one snack your child can open without a grown-up.

      At the table

      Slice lengthwise, lay it open, and load one raisin passenger aboard.

      What it teaches

      Independence at snack time — a word attached to a self-serve skill.

      Getting it on paper

      Standard portrait is fine; bananas are naturally off-model.

      Tip for today

      Let the peel fail sometimes; unwrapping is half the lesson.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Banana lesson on the Learning Path.

      One word, two lessons

      This card names the fruit; over in Look & Learn the same banana becomes a game — pretend to peel it, say the word — and at lunchtime it counts itself in the Cafeteria room: one banana, one finger, among sixty-two tray foods.

      Orange Flashcard for Preschoolers

      A round orange with a green leaf — the only food whose name is also its color. The word orange sits under it, and the smell begins before the peel is even off.

      Download card ↓

      Teaching tips

      What this card does

      Labels the fruit that arrives in its own wrapping and smells like morning.

      At the table

      Hold the half up like a smile, then eat the smile.

      What it teaches

      Smell, peel, share — a small fruit with a full curriculum.

      Getting it on paper

      Print it bright; oranges resent grey printing.

      Tip for today

      Sniff palms together afterwards; the review writes itself.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Orange lesson on the Learning Path.

      Strawberry Flashcard for Preschoolers

      A bright red strawberry with its green crown and its seeds showing — the only fruit that wears its seeds on the outside. The word strawberry sits under it, looking exactly like summer.

      Download card ↓

      Teaching tips

      What this card does

      Captures the summer fruit with the leafy hat and the too-many seeds.

      At the table

      Push a straw up from the bottom and the leafy hat pops off whole.

      What it teaches

      Noticing details — seeds, hats, hearts — is the observation habit starting.

      Getting it on paper

      One for the kitchen, one for wherever berries get discussed.

      Tip for today

      Straws must be the wide kind; engineering has standards.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Strawberry lesson on the Learning Path.

      One word, two lessons

      Here the strawberry is for naming; in the Look & Learn deck the same red strawberry asks for its colour and its shape, and the Cafeteria room shows off its outside seeds and counts to four.

      Grapes Flashcard for Preschoolers

      A whole bunch of purple grapes — one word for many little balls. The word grapes sits under them, and grapes are the classic sharing food: one for you, one for me.

      Download card ↓

      Teaching tips

      What this card does

      Covers a whole bunch in one small word, which feels like a bargain.

      At the table

      Try them cold from the freezer, cut small — frosty little sorbets.

      What it teaches

      Sharing words grow wherever a whole bunch needs dividing.

      Getting it on paper

      Small print sizes survive; grapes are the set's compact model.

      Tip for today

      Freeze sparingly; supply never survives the demand anyway.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Grapes lesson on the Learning Path.

      One word, two lessons

      This card is for naming the bunch; the Look & Learn class plays the describing game instead, and the Cafeteria room points at one grape inside the crowd and counts three into a cup.

      Watermelon Flashcard for Preschoolers

      A watermelon slice with green rind, red flesh and shiny black seeds — the biggest word on the biggest fruit. The word watermelon sits under it, ready for the hottest day.

      Download card ↓

      Teaching tips

      What this card does

      Names the biggest fruit in the shop and the heaviest guest at the table.

      At the table

      Count the dark stripes out loud first; the eating may begin after.

      What it teaches

      Summer brings the big words — heavy, huge, striped, refreshing.

      Getting it on paper

      Print it large; nothing about this card should apologise.

      Tip for today

      Put newspaper down first; this fruit answers to nobody.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Watermelon lesson on the Learning Path.

      Pineapple Flashcard for Preschoolers

      A golden pineapple with a spiky green crown — the fanciest hat in the fruit bowl. The word pineapple sits under it, bumpy on the outside and sweet on the inside.

      Download card ↓

      Teaching tips

      What this card does

      Explains the crowned guest who takes up half the fruit bowl.

      At the table

      Pass it around the table once — every hand confirms, definitely spiky.

      What it teaches

      Texture words — spiky, bumpy, tough — need exactly this specimen.

      Getting it on paper

      Thick paper helps; pineapples dent everything, including cards.

      Tip for today

      Own the spiky verdict yourself first; bravery is copied.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Pineapple lesson on the Learning Path.

      Mango Flashcard for Preschoolers

      A golden-yellow mango with a green leaf — the sweetest word to say slowly: mmmm-mango. The word mango sits under it, blushing orange where the sun would have caught it.

      Download card ↓

      Teaching tips

      What this card does

      Introduces the tropical one — the fruit that makes spoons necessary.

      At the table

      Wash the stone afterwards and stand it in the middle of the table.

      What it teaches

      Soft-when-ready language teaches ripeness, patience and gentle squeezing.

      Getting it on paper

      Any paper works — the card outlasts the fruit, whatever it is.

      Tip for today

      Gentle squeezes only; fruit should feel like a cheek.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Mango lesson on the Learning Path.

      Carrot Flashcard for Preschoolers

      An orange carrot with a leafy green top — the vegetable that grows hiding underground. The word carrot sits under it, pointy at the bottom and leafy at the top.

      Download card ↓

      Teaching tips

      What this card does

      Points to the crunchiest resident of the drawer and its loudest fans.

      At the table

      Ask for sticks or coins tonight — shape requests count as vegetable talk.

      What it teaches

      Crunch is a word, and loudly proving it is learning.

      Getting it on paper

      Colour settings on — economy mode makes famously sad carrots.

      Tip for today

      Loud crunching is the point; shush nobody at this table.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Carrot lesson on the Learning Path.

      One word, two lessons

      Naming the carrot is this card’s whole job; Look & Learn adds the move — pretend to pull a carrot from the ground — and the Cafeteria room counts it: three carrots and a rabbit crunch.

      Potato Flashcard for Preschoolers

      A brown potato with little spots — lumpy, bumpy and proud of it. The word potato sits under it, and potatoes grow underground just like carrots, hiding from the birds.

      Download card ↓

      Teaching tips

      What this card does

      Prints the underground hero behind chips, mash and every good Sunday.

      At the table

      Build a small mash mountain and send the fork up as first climber.

      What it teaches

      Same plant, many dinners — variety gets its first example.

      Getting it on paper

      Plain paper suits the humblest card in the set.

      Tip for today

      Serve the mountain edible; no tidy-up lecture required.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Potato lesson on the Learning Path.

      Tomato Flashcard for Preschoolers

      A round red tomato with a little green star on top — shiny as a bauble. The word tomato sits under it, and tomatoes live in salads, sauces and lunchboxes everywhere.

      Download card ↓

      Teaching tips

      What this card does

      Files the red one whose food group is genuinely up for debate.

      At the table

      Compare a windowsill tomato with a fridge tomato — one of them is wrong.

      What it teaches

      One food, two categories — categories bend, and children notice.

      Getting it on paper

      Pair it with the apple card — the debate deserves both sides.

      Tip for today

      Let both answers stand tonight; the argument is doing its job.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Tomato lesson on the Learning Path.

      Cucumber Flashcard for Preschoolers

      A long green cucumber — the coolest vegetable in the bowl. The word cucumber sits under it, long and smooth with bumpy skin like its cousin the watermelon.

      Download card ↓

      Teaching tips

      What this card does

      Presents the coolest customer in the crisper, word and all.

      At the table

      Lay two slices into tonight's sandwiches — the crunch department reporting in.

      What it teaches

      Cool and crisp become describing words with evidence at lunch.

      Getting it on paper

      Prints crisply in green or grey; the cucumber forgives both.

      Tip for today

      Cold from the fridge is the whole point; say so at serving.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Cucumber lesson on the Learning Path.

      Broccoli Flashcard for Preschoolers

      A green broccoli that looks exactly like a tiny tree — the vegetable children most love to pretend with. The word broccoli sits under it, all leafy and lumpy at the top.

      Download card ↓

      Teaching tips

      What this card does

      Trains the eye to see a vegetable that looks suspiciously like a tree.

      At the table

      Give each floret a dip and let the little trees go swimming.

      What it teaches

      Tree talk now, plant parts later — botany starts at dinner.

      Getting it on paper

      Full-page printing suits it; forests need room.

      Tip for today

      Dips count as parenting wins — yoghurt, hummus, whatever survives.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Broccoli lesson on the Learning Path.

      Corn Flashcard for Preschoolers

      A corn cob in its green husk, kernels lined up like little yellow bricks. The word corn sits under it, and every kernel is a seed that pops or crunches.

      Download card ↓

      Teaching tips

      What this card does

      Documents the vegetable that arrives in its own packaging, butter optional.

      At the table

      Twirl it slowly while you eat — corn is a homemade rotisserie.

      What it teaches

      Names a food that arrives wearing its own jacket.

      Getting it on paper

      Yellow toner optional — the word does the colouring.

      Tip for today

      Argue your twirling method openly; consistency is for other vegetables.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Corn lesson on the Learning Path.

      Onion Flashcard for Preschoolers

      A round brown onion, papery on the outside and full of secrets inside. The word onion sits under it — the vegetable that hides layer under layer.

      Download card ↓

      Teaching tips

      What this card does

      Warns, in the friendliest way, about the kitchen's most emotional vegetable.

      At the table

      Announce who cried first; someone always blames the steam.

      What it teaches

      Layers as a concept — onions are where nested thinking starts.

      Getting it on paper

      No tears at the printer — that happens at the chopping board.

      Tip for today

      Wash little hands afterwards; eyes will thank everyone later.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Onion lesson on the Learning Path.

      Pumpkin Flashcard for Preschoolers

      A big orange pumpkin with a sturdy stem — the largest vegetable on the cards and a season all by itself. The word pumpkin sits under it, round and ribbed and ready.

      Download card ↓

      Teaching tips

      What this card does

      Carries the loudest month of the year in one orange word.

      At the table

      Guess its weight, then weigh it — every kitchen scale loves a pumpkin.

      What it teaches

      Big fruit, big seeds, big words — autumn measures everything.

      Getting it on paper

      Heavy paper again — pumpkins are not lightweight company.

      Tip for today

      Draw the face early; October arrives faster than printers do.

      Teach it, step by step

      Want the full walkthrough? Open the Pumpkin lesson on the Learning Path.
